objections.claim: For any branch name containing `/`, the fresh-create guard in §3.2 checks the wrong ref and therefore does not apply to exactly the case where the flattening hazard exists. `setup-worktree.sh` creates the branch as `SAFE_NAME` (`tr '/' '-'`), so the only branch that can ever be pushed and shadowed is the flattened one; §4.1 mandates that "the `ls-remote` check uses the real branch name", which is a ref nothing in this system ever creates. The TypeScript-side check on `s.branch` will always get exit 2 (continue) for a slash-scoped scheme, and if the script-side check follows the same "real branch name" wording it will also pass while `git worktree add -b <flattened>` shadows a pushed flattened branch — reintroducing, silently, the precise divergence this spec exists to close.
objections.evidence: §3.2 ("`git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <branch>`"), §4.1 ("Branch names with `/`. The slug flattens them for the path; the `ls-remote` check uses the real branch name"), against `setup-worktree.sh`'s `SAFE_NAME=$(echo "$NAME" | tr '/' '-')` and `git worktree add -b "${SAFE_NAME}"`, and `worktree-ensure.ts`'s `slash-scoped` scheme producing `feature/<issue>-<slug>`.
objections.predicted_consequence: on a repo using the `slash-scoped` branch_naming scheme, a previously pushed `feature-FAFF-9-x` is shadowed by a fresh create with no refusal and no diagnostic — the DONE item "A fresh create refuses when `origin/<branch>` exists" is vacuously satisfied while the failure it describes still occurs.

objections.claim: §3.1 specifies the refusal against "the path `<root>/<branch-slug>`", but the script computes the worktree path as `WT_ROOT/${SAFE_NAME}` where `SAFE_NAME` flattens `/` to `-` (setup-worktree.sh: `SAFE_NAME=$(echo "$NAME" | tr '/' '-')`). Under the `slash-scoped` branch_naming scheme (`feature/<issue>-<slug>`) these are different strings: a TypeScript check against the unflattened `<root>/feature/faff-9-x` never sees a symlink planted at the flattened `<root>/feature-faff-9-x`. The bundled script's own check covers the bundled-script path, and the step-6 root assert still refuses an escaped worktree, so nothing exploitable ships — but a project-supplied `scripts/setup-worktree.sh` that does its own path computation gets only a check against a path it never creates, i.e. the §3.1 TypeScript floor is vacuous for exactly the case it was added to cover.
objections.evidence: spec §3.1 ("the path `<root>/<branch-slug>`"); `setup-worktree.sh` `SAFE_NAME=$(echo "$NAME" | tr '/' '-')`; spec §3.1 Chosen rationale ("the TypeScript check covers a project-specific `scripts/setup-worktree.sh`"); worktree-ensure.ts `resolveBranch` (`slash-scoped` → `feature/${issueSlug}`).
objections.predicted_consequence: with a project setup script, a symlink at the flattened worktree path is not refused before provisioning; the worktree registers outside the root and the issue parks `root-outside` on every drain until manual cleanup (the exact pre-existing failure this spec's §3.1 claims to close).

objections.claim: §3.2 has `freshCreate` check the flattened name and, when different, the unflattened branch name, refusing if *either* exists, with detail `{ reason: "remote branch exists", branch }` — a single branch field. `git ls-remote` exits 0 when any pattern matches; with both patterns passed (or two calls), the result cannot say which ref matched. The spec then routes on this field: §4.1 requires graft Step 3 to "surface the message names the branch", and the stated rationale is that a human can "delete it or resume deliberately". A surfaced name that may be the wrong one of the two sends the operator at the wrong ref.
objections.evidence: §3.2 ("it checks both, and refuses if either exists", detail `{ reason, branch }`); §4.1 ("the surfaced message names the branch").
objections.predicted_consequence: an operator following the surfaced `detail.branch` deletes or inspects the wrong remote branch (e.g. deletes `feature/faff-9-x` when the match was the flattened `faff-9-x`), leaving the actual shadowing branch in place and the next drain parked again.
objections.disposition_rationale: Fixed in place after round 2; not re-reviewed. Accepted by the operator after round 2.

objections.claim: §3.3 names two distinct failure branches in the script — root-lookup failure and no-`faff`-binary-at-all — and DONE item 3 requires both ("exits 1 with a named error when the root lookup fails or no `faff` resolves"). Only the first is covered: scenario 4 and the §4.2 test both drive a stub whose `worktree-root` exits 1. Nothing anywhere decides the no-binary branch, which has its own distinct error string (`setup-worktree: no faff binary resolvable…`).
